subject.title: feat(plugins): add exact-profile provider usage reads

question: Should OpenClaw publish `runtime.providerUsage.read()` as a stable plugin SDK capability for trusted plugins, or keep exact-profile usage resolution internal until an approved product caller and long-term contract are defined?
rationale: The implementation adds a new compatibility-sensitive plugin API at the credential and agent-scope boundary. Tests can validate mechanics, but they cannot determine whether this permanent public capability, its trust assumptions, and its supported use cases are the desired product contract.

options.title: Defer the public SDK API
options.body: Keep exact-profile resolution internal or tied to an approved feature until an owner defines the plugin permission, privacy, and support contract.

options.title: Sponsor the stable API
options.body: Approve this narrow token-free API, require explicit contract and upgrade documentation, and proceed after real-provider proof verifies its exact-profile guarantees.

recommendation.title: Defer the public SDK API
recommendation.body: Keep exact-profile resolution internal or tied to an approved feature until an owner defines the plugin permission, privacy, and support contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the permanent core plugin SDK and provider-auth boundary rather than a mechanical branch repair.
